mfa_code.description: Multi-factor authentication code. Required when MFA is enabled for the user account.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking. Optional field - server can extract IP from request, but client may provide it for SSR scenarios. Used to populate connection metadata in authentication sessions.

href.description: Connection URL when the session was created. Required for authentication operations to track connection context.

referrer.description: Referrer URL when the session was created. Required for authentication operations to track connection referral source.

ITodoUser.IRefresh.description: Request body schema for refreshing authentication tokens in the Todo application. This DTO represents the refresh token needed to obtain new authentication credentials without re-entering login credentials. Users submit their currently valid refresh token from their existing authentication session to receive fresh access and refresh tokens, extending their authenticated session while maintaining security boundaries. This process implements automatic session continuation for improved user experience by allowing issued access tokens to be refreshed automatically when they expire.

refresh_token.description: Current valid refresh token extracted from the existing authentication session. This token is validated against the user's active session data in todo_user_sessions table and the IAuthorizationToken structure to ensure it's still valid and not expired. The token serves as the credential exchange mechanism that proves the user's existing authenticated state, enabling the system to issue new tokens without requiring password re-authentication while maintaining secure session management as specified in the authentication requirements.

ITodoUser.description: Registered users with comprehensive authentication fields supporting password reset, account security, and multi-factor authentication. Each user account is associated with a unique email address and encrypted password hash for secure authentication. User details are returned for authenticated users accessing their own data, excluding sensitive authentication data like passwords and tokens from API responses while maintaining complete audit trail capabilities through soft deletion support.

id.description: Primary Key from todo_users.id. Unique identifier for the user account

email.description: User's email address for authentication and communication from todo_users.email. Must be unique across all registered users.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created from todo_users.created_at. Automatically set on registration.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated from todo_users.updated_at. Automatically updated on any account changes.

mfa_enabled.description: Whether multi-factor authentication is enabled from todo_users.mfa_enabled. Defaults to false for new accounts.

failed_login_attempts.description: Number of consecutive failed login attempts from todo_users.failed_login_attempts. Used to implement account lockout protection after 5 failed attempts as specified in security requirements.

locked_until.description: Timestamp when account lockout expires after failed login attempts from todo_users.locked_until. Implements time-based account recovery for security protection.

tasks_count.description: Number of tasks associated with this user account calculated from todo_tasks table relationship

ITodoUser.IPasswordResetRequest.description:
Request body for initiating password reset for todo application users. This DTO captures the email address of the user requesting password recovery.

The email address is the unique identifier used to look up the user's account in the todo_users table. When a valid email is provided, the system generates a secure reset token and sets the reset_password_expires timestamp to 30 minutes in the future as specified in the requirements.

This is the first step in the password reset workflow, enabling users who have forgotten their passwords to regain access to their accounts and todo lists. The system implements proper security measures to prevent abuse while ensuring legitimate users can recover access to their task management functionality.

email.description: User's email address for password reset request. This must be a valid email address associated with an existing account in the todo_users table. The email serves as the unique identifier to locate the user's account and initiate the password reset process with proper security validation.

ITodoUser.IPasswordResetResponse.description:
Response confirming that password reset request was processed successfully. The response provides user feedback about the password reset initiation without revealing security-sensitive information to prevent account enumeration attacks.

The confirmation message helps build user trust by clearly communicating what to expect next in the password recovery process. Users will receive a password reset link via email if the email address exists in the system, maintaining security best practices by not confirming whether an email exists.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating that password reset request is being processed. This message provides user-friendly feedback about the next steps in the password recovery process. The message maintains security by not confirming whether the email address exists in the system to prevent account enumeration attacks.

ITodoUser.IPasswordResetConfirm.description: Request body for completing the password reset process. This DTO captures the validation token, new password, and password confirmation required for secure password reset completion. The token links to the user's specific reset request, ensuring tokens can only be used once within the 30-minute validity window defined in the todo_users.reset_password_token table structure.

confirm_password.description: Confirmation of the new password to ensure accuracy. Must exactly match the password field to prevent typing errors during the password selection process.

password.description: The new password for the user account. Must meet security requirements as defined in the system's password policy. This will be securely hashed and stored in the password_hash field, replacing the existing password.

reset_password_token.description: The password reset token sent to the user's email. This unique token is valid for 30 minutes from the time of the password reset request. It is used to verify the user's identity during the password reset process and can only be used once. The token is associated with the user's todo_users.reset_password_token field in the database.

ITodoUser.IPasswordResetConfirmResponse.description: Response body confirming the result of the password reset operation. Returns a boolean success indicator to provide immediate feedback about whether the password was successfully reset. On success, the user's old password is replaced and cannot be recovered. On failure, users receive clear feedback about what went wrong so they can retry the process.

success.description: Indicates whether the password reset operation was successful. True if the reset token was valid, the passwords match security requirements, and the new password was successfully saved. False indicates failure due to invalid token, expired token, or password validation errors.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated guest user, corresponds to todo_guests.id. This UUID serves as the primary key for guest session management and is used to track temporary visitor sessions throughout the application lifecycle. The identifier enables secure session verification and resource association.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guest access was created from todo_guests.created_at. This represents the moment when temporary visitor access was granted, used for audit trails, session management, and determining guest session expiry. The timestamp follows ISO 8601 format with timezone support.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when guest session was last modified or settings updated. Tracks any changes to guest session configuration or status updates. For guest sessions, this primarily updates when session parameters are refreshed or extended.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when guest access was revoked or expired. Null for active guest sessions. This field enables soft deletion of guest records while maintaining audit trails. Temporary guest sessions are automatically cleaned up after a configurable timeout period to prevent accumulation.

ITodoGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Guest authorization response containing temporary session credentials for preview functionality. This response type enables unauthenticated visitors to explore basic todo application features through temporary access, serving as a user acquisition mechanism that demonstrates the service's simplicity and value proposition.

Guest sessions are designed to be lightweight, temporary, and non-invasive. They allow potential customers to experience the application's core functionality without registration friction. The response includes the guest account creation timestamp, session metadata, and JWT authentication tokens for subsequent secure API requests.

This authorization flow corresponds to public guest join operations at /auth/guest/join endpoint, providing immediate access to preview todo task management features. The temporary nature encourages user conversion while maintaining security boundaries through appropriate access controls.

page.description: Page number for pagination, required to specify which page of results to retrieve, starting from page 1.

limit.description: Number of items per page for pagination control. Used to control the number of configuration entries returned per request, ranging from 1 to 100 items per page with a default value of 20.

When false, filters for user-managed configurations. False enables filtering for user-accessible configuration parameters while null shows all configurations regardless of system protection status.

ITodoConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for system configuration queries with pagination support. This request DTO enables administrators to query configuration settings with advanced filtering including text search capabilities, type filtering, and system-level flag filtering for comprehensive configuration management.

Configuration management is critical for application-wide settings that control system behavior including feature toggles, operational limits, display preferences, and integration parameters. This operation enables technical staff to efficiently locate specific configuration entries, identify configuration-related issues, and maintain consistent configuration across the application infrastructure.

The filtering system supports complex queries with multiple criteria including string search against configuration keys and descriptions using PostgreSQL GIN indexing for performance optimization. This enables administrators to manage system configuration through a unified interface with pagination support for large result sets.

IBoolean.description: Boolean type for filtering flags and boolean configuration values

IString.description: String type for text search queries and configuration type filters in the Todo application configuration system. This type enables flexible text-based filtering of system configuration settings through search operations against configuration keys and descriptions. The string format supports partial matching and typo tolerance through PostgreSQL GIN indexing with trigram operations, allowing administrators to efficiently locate specific configuration entries by searching for relevant keywords or phrases within configuration metadata.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this configuration setting.

key.description: Unique configuration key identifier used to reference the setting in application code.

value.description: Configuration value stored as string. Can contain JSON data for complex configuration objects.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the configuration was last modified.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the configuration was soft deleted. Null if the configuration is active.

System-wide configuration settings that store application-wide settings and preferences. This table provides a flexible key-value store for various configuration parameters that can be adjusted without requiring code changes or deployments.

This table stores configuration settings that can control system behavior including feature toggles, operational limits, display preferences, and integration settings. All configurations support soft deletion to maintain audit trails and enable recovery if needed.

ITodoConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating new system configuration settings. This DTO enables administrators to add configuration parameters that control various aspects of the todo application behavior.

The configuration system supports flexible parameter management through key-value pairs with type validation and system-level protection. Each configuration entry serves as a building block for application behavior control, enabling dynamic adjustments without requiring code deployments or system restarts.

description.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and impact of this configuration setting. Required for documentation and context for future administrators managing the configuration system.

is_system.description: System-level protection flag. When true, the configuration requires elevated permissions for future modifications and is protected from unauthorized changes. System configurations should be used for critical parameters that affect application core functionality.

ITodoConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Update data for modifying an existing configuration setting. All fields are optional, allowing selective updates to specific configuration properties while preserving others.

This type is used when updating configuration values through the administrative interface. The value must be compatible with the specified type field to ensure data consistency across the application.

description.description: Updated human-readable description explaining what this configuration setting controls.

is_system.description: Updated system flag indicating whether this is a system-level configuration. Only allowed if user has appropriate permissions.

type.description: Updated configuration type (string, number, boolean, JSON). Should match the format of the provided value field.

value.description: Updated configuration value stored as a string. Supports JSON data for complex objects. Must be compatible with the existing type field.

ITodoGuest.description:
Represent temporary visitor access session in the Todo application allowing unauthenticated users to preview basic functionality without registration. Guest user functionality serves the user acquisition funnel by enabling unregistered visitors to experience core task management features while maintaining security boundaries through session-based access control.

The guest user entity enables the freemium business model by allowing potential customers to experience the application's simplicity and core functionality before committing to full user registration. Guest sessions are lightweight, temporary by design, and include basic session tracking to monitor user acquisition funnel performance while respecting user anonymity and conversion patterns.

Each guest session provides limited access to todo task management features including viewing sample tasks, understanding the user interface, and experiencing task completion workflows. The system maintains audit trails through IP address tracking and session management while preventing unauthorized access to user-specific functionality like creating tasks or managing personal accounts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the guest visitor session. This UUID serves as the primary key for the todo_guests table and enables session management across guest operations. The identifier supports tracking of visitor interactions while maintaining anonymity and enables temporary access control for demonstration features within the application's cookie governance and session isolation boundaries.

created_at.description: Timestamp when guest access was first created and granted through todo_guests.created_at field in PostgreSQL database. This timestamp records the moment temporary visitor access was established from server-side session creation, used for session expiry calculations and user acquisition analytics. The field follows ISO 8601 format with PostgreSQL timestamptz precision for accurate visitor pattern analysis across timezone variants.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when guest session was last modified or settings updated through todo_guests.updated_at field. Tracks changes to guest session configuration or status updates including session extension operations or access permission modifications. This timestamp enables session lifecycle management and provides audit trails for guest visitor activities within the todo application demonstration interface for privacy compliance and usage analytics.

oneOf.description: Active guest session with no deletion timestamp indicates normal operations and running demonstration access for user onboarding funnel conversion
Soft deletion timestamp using todo_guests.deleted_at field indicates when guest access was intentionally revoked or expired due to cleanup policies for privacy compliance

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when guest access was revoked, expired, or cleaned up through natural session management or privacy data retention policies. Null values indicate active guest sessions with ongoing demonstration access. Soft deletion enables privacy compliance and audit trail maintenance while automatically cleaning up expired guest session records according to data retention policies specified in privacy regulations.

ITodoTask.description: Individual todo tasks that users can create, complete, and manage. Each task represents a single unit of work that can be completed and tracked over time. Tasks are associated with users and support simple completion status tracking.

referrer.description: Referrer URL when the session was created. Required for self-authentication operations to track referral source.

ITodoUserSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a user session containing essential session identifiers and metadata for session management, display, and audit purposes. This type provides comprehensive session overview for administrative interfaces, user activity monitoring, network security analysis, and session reference lookups while maintaining data minimization principles.

The summary structure is optimized for high-frequency access patterns in authentication systems where administrators need to review User Session activity across multiple security scenarios. It identifies sessions by unique identifier while including key creation and status information needed for immediate security decisions, threat detection, and compliance auditing without exposing sensitive user authentication data.

Key Business Contexts:
- Network Security: IP address tracking enables intrusion detection and geographic access analysis
- Audit Compliance: Detailed session timestamps support regulatory requirements and forensic investigation
- Traffic Analysis: Referrer URLs provide user journey insights and acquisition source identification
- Session Management: Connection URLs track initial access points for detailed security monitoring
- Administrative Oversight: Enables efficient session review across suspicious activity patterns
- Performance Optimization: Minimal data exposure reduces network overhead while maintaining complete audit capability

Session Management Operations:
- Security professionals use this for reviewing active sessions across suspicious activity patterns
- System administrators monitor session health and identify potential security threats
- Compliance officers utilize session records for regulatory audit trail requirements
- Support teams use session data for troubleshooting user access issues

The structure balances comprehensive session oversight with privacy protection by excluding sensitive authentication tokens while preserving critical network and timing information needed for security analysis and audit compliance.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user session. Automatically generated UUID serving as the primary key for session records and used for session identification in authentication contexts. This identifier enables secure session verification, audit trail tracking, cross-system session correlation, and efficient database indexing for high-frequency session lookup operations across administrative dashboards and security monitoring tools.

ip.description: IP address of the user's connection. Provides network-level identification for security analysis including geographic location detection, threat intelligence correlation, IP reputation checking, and detailed access pattern analysis. Enables security audit functionality, access control verification, lateral movement detection, and integration with network security tools for comprehensive connection security analysis across enterprise environments.

href.description: Connection URL when the session was created. Records the specific page or endpoint accessed during session initialization for usage analytics, redirect handling, user experience tracking, service quality monitoring, and detailed security context tracking. Provides foundational data for user journey analysis, A/B testing, feature adoption metrics, and understanding how users discover and interact with authentication flows.

referrer.description: Referrer URL when the session was created. Logs the previous webpage that directed the user to create this session, enabling comprehensive traffic source tracking, user journey analysis, marketing campaign effectiveness measurement, affiliate program monitoring, SEO performance analysis, and security monitoring for unusual referral patterns that might indicate automated attacks or suspicious traffic sources.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Uses PostGIS timestamptz format for precise time tracking of authentication events with timezone support, ensuring audit trail accuracy across all geographical regions. Provides critical foundation for session age calculations, auto-expiration logic, security timeout enforcement, and compliance with time-sensitive regulatory requirements including geographical data residency and access time limitations.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Null if the session remains active. Automatically calculated based on configurable TTL settings that enforce automatic session cleanup, security timeout requirements, and administrative session management policies. This field enables automated session lifecycle management, security timeout enforcement, scheduled cleanup operations, and compliance with organizational session duration policies while providing clear session state information for administrative dashboards and security monitoring workflows.

ITodoUserSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating user sessions with comprehensive administrative search capabilities designed for security monitoring, audit compliance, and detailed user activity analysis. This request format supports complex queries that enable network security analysts, system administrators, compliance officers, and support teams to find sessions based on multiple security-critical criteria including IP address filtering, creation date ranges, session status analysis, geographic access patterns, and detailed connection metadata tracking.

The request structure is specifically optimized for enterprise-level authentication security monitoring where administrators need granular control over session analysis and real-time threat detection capabilities. It provides essential tools for investigating security incidents, monitoring user access patterns, conducting compliance audits, and supporting user troubleshooting across multi-tenant authentication systems.

Key Security Monitoring Scenarios:
- Threat Detection: IP-based filtering enables identification of suspicious access patterns, geographic anomalies, and potential account compromise
- Audit Investigation: Date range filtering supports forensic analysis of authentication events and compliance reporting requirements
- Access Analytics: Referrer URL tracking provides insights into traffic sources, user acquisition, and potential security vulnerabilities
- Geographic Verification: IP address filtering combined with session metadata enables detection of impossible user movements between geographically distant locations
- Session Lifecycle Management: Active vs expired session filtering supports operational session cleanup and resource optimization
- Automated Response: Comprehensive filtering enables integration with security tools for automatic threat response and access control enforcement

Administrative Capabilities:
- Network administrators filter by IP addresses to investigate potential security incidents or implement geo-blocking policies
- Security teams use referrer analysis to understand traffic sources and identify potential phishing attacks or social engineering attempts
- Compliance officers analyze session creation patterns and connection metadata to ensure regulatory requirements are met
- Support teams leverage session data for troubleshooting user authentication issues and providing detailed login history
- System operators monitor session health and implement session management policies through comprehensive filtering and search capabilities

The filtering system balances security requirements for detailed session analysis with performance optimization principles by supporting efficient database queries, maintaining reasonable pagination limits, and providing comprehensive result sorting options for security investigations and administrative reporting workflows.

page.description: Page number for pagination results, starting from 1 for the first page. This parameter enables systematic browsing through large session datasets that exceed standard result limits, supporting comprehensive security investigations that may span thousands of individual authentication events while maintaining consistent performance across administrative dashboards and security monitoring interfaces.

limit.description: Number of items per page for pagination results, with a maximum of 100 items per request to balance comprehensive data access with server performance optimization. This limit supports efficient database query execution while providing sufficient detail for security analysis, administrative reporting, and compliance documentation across enterprise authentication systems with potentially large user bases.

ip.description: Filter sessions by specific IP address for security monitoring and forensic audit purposes. This filtering enables comprehensive investigation of specific connection sources including threat intelligence correlation against known malicious IP addresses, geographic verification to detect impossible user movements, network access pattern analysis, and detailed security event correlation with other authentication and authorization systems across the enterprise security infrastructure.

referrer.description: Filter sessions by referrer URL to understand traffic sources and comprehensive user acquisition patterns. This filtering provides critical insights into user journey mapping, traffic source security analysis, advertising campaign effectiveness measurement, SEO performance tracking, affiliate program monitoring, and identification of potentially suspicious traffic patterns that might indicate automated attacks, social engineering attempts, or unauthorized access attempts through exploit-based mitigation techniques.

created_after.description: Filter sessions created after this timestamp to find recent sessions or conduct precise time-range analysis for forensic investigations. This parameter enables security teams to narrow analysis windows around security incidents, track session creation patterns across specific time domains, and implement automated session monitoring workflows that trigger alerts when unusual authentication patterns emerge within critical business timeframes or during heightened security monitoring periods.

created_before.description: Filter sessions created before this timestamp to exclude newer sessions and enable comprehensive historical analysis across authentication events. This filtering supports audit trail construction spanning extended time periods, enables compliance with data retention policies by identifying sessions within specific regulatory timeframes, and allows security teams to analyze authentication patterns across extended investigation timelines for comprehensive incident response and threat correlation analysis.

expired.description: Filter sessions by status where true restricts results to expired sessions only, false shows only active sessions, and null includes all sessions regardless of expiration status. This filtering enables administrators to focus on specific session lifecycle stages including active session monitoring for operational session management, expired session analysis for cleanup policies and resource optimization, and comprehensive session state analysis across administrative dashboards that monitor authentication health and enforce organizational timeout policies.

sort_by.description: Sort order parameter controlling result organization, supporting values: 'created_at' for chronological ordering ideal for time-based investigations, 'ip' for IP address grouping that facilitates network security analysis and geographic correlation, 'expired_at' for expiration-focused analysis that supports session lifecycle management and cleanup operations. Default sorting by creation time provides chronological authentication event tracking while specialized sorting enables focused analysis approaches for different security monitoring and administrative oversight use cases across enterprise authentication systems.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for results in ascending order showing oldest sessions, events with lowest values, or alphanumeric ordering starting from A. Enables chronological progression analysis, geographic ordering, and systematic session enumeration for audit trail construction across compliance frameworks that require sequential documentation and alignment with temporal authentication event sequences across distributed systems.

Sort direction for results in descending order showing newest sessions, events with highest values, or reverse alphanumeric ordering from Z. This option facilitates immediate threat detection by presenting most recent authentication events first, supports investigation workflows prioritizing current security concerns, and enables administrative dashboards to display critical information in reverse chronological order that matches enterprise security monitoring standards and incident response workflows.

sort_order.description: Sort direction parameter controlling the organizational approach for paginated result presentation showing either ascending or descending order based on the specific sort_by field selection. Descending order (newest first) enables immediate access to most recent authentication events facilitating real-time security monitoring, while ascending order (oldest first) supports chronological investigation workflows and comprehensive audit trail construction across authentication event sequences spanning extended time domains.

ITodoGuest.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for guest visitor settings - enables modification of temporary guest session configuration for demonstration purposes. Guest users can update their temporary session preferences while maintaining anonymous access to preview todo functionality. This DTO represents the request payload for modifying guest sessions and does NOT require authentication context (guest users are unauthenticated).

All fields are optional to allow partial updates - users can modify specific guest settings without affecting other configuration. The endpoint should validate business logic such as extending guest session validity periods within reasonable limits to prevent abuse of demonstration access.

This update operation supports session management by allowing modification of guest session expiration timestamps, enabling dynamic control over how long demonstration access persists for better visitor experience.

href.description: Connection URL - optional update for guest session creation context, used to track demonstration session origin

ip.description: IP address - optional update for geographical session tracking during guest demonstrations

referrer.description: Referrer URL - optional update to track traffic sources for guest users accessing demonstration functionality

expired_at.description: Updated timestamp when the guest session expires. Setting this allows extension of demonstration access periods. Null indicates indefinite session (not recommended for security). The timestamp should be managed within reasonable security boundaries to prevent excessive demonstration access duration while ensuring positive user experience.

ITodoGuestSession.description: Guest session tracking entity for temporary access to the todo application without registration. Guest sessions allow unregistered users to preview basic functionality while maintaining security isolation through comprehensive connection metadata tracking. Each session includes IP address, URL references, and temporal information for audit purposes, security monitoring, and session lifecycle management.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the guest session using UUID format for distributed system compatibility

todo_guest_id.description: The guest user's id who owns this session. Foreign key reference to todo_guests.id maintaining proper relationship constraints

ip.description: IP address of the guest's connection for audit purposes and geographic location detection enabling security analysis

href.description: Connection URL when the session was created. Records the specific page accessed during session initialization for usage analytics

referrer.description: Referrer URL when the session was created. Logs the previous webpage that directed the user to create this session for traffic source analysis

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created using PostGIS timestamptz format for precise time tracking with timezone support

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the guest session expires. Null if the session remains active. Automatically calculated based on configurable TTL settings for security timeout enforcement

ITodoGuestSession.IRequest.description: Request DTO for guest session operations including refresh and metadata updates. Used for maintaining temporary guest access and updating session information during the guest user's interaction with the application while preserving security boundaries.

ip.description: IP address of the guest's connection for audit purposes. Optional field to update session tracking information

href.description: Connection URL when the session was created. Required to track the original access point for the guest session

referrer.description: Referrer URL when the session was created. Required to understand how guest users are discovering the application

ITodoTask.ISecure.description: Secure response DTO representing a todo task with all accessible fields exposed. This comprehensive view includes task identity, description, completion status, business workflow status, temporal tracking, and user ownership information. The ISecure variant is used for detailed task views where the requesting user owns the task, providing complete information including sensitive connection metadata if needed for auditing or detailed display purposes.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the todo task.

todo_user_id.description: User who created and owns this task.

description.description: Task description content up to 500 characters.

completed.description: Completion status of the task. False indicates incomplete, true indicates completed.

business_status.description: Business workflow status of the task. Values: pending, processing, completed.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the task was created. Automatically set when task is first added.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the task was last modified. Updated automatically on any change to the task.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the task was marked as completed. Only set when task transitions to completed state.
